header: Private editorial working note, 17 October 2026. **REQUIRES HUMAN SIGN-OFF.** This is not approved visitor copy. No changes to `inductees/hope/copy.md` are authorized by this note.

IHH starting page: [bob-hope](https://immigranthallofhonor.org/inductees/inductee-bob-hope/), retrieved during this review. Line references identify the retrieved text view, not a stable page anchor. L27.claim: Entertained US troops on the USO Tours for 50 years (1941 – 1991)
evidence: After entertaining American troops at March Field in Riverside, California in 1941, Hope joined the USO
flying around the world to perform for troops during the KOREAN WAR, VIETNAM, and the PERSIAN GULF WAR
L27.note: The 1941 start is confirmed. The quoted text names the Persian Gulf War but does not state the 1991 end year, so “1991” and “50 years” rest on inference. Status revised 17 Oct 2026 from CONFIRMED.

L28.claim: Hosted The Bob Hope Show (Radio: 1938 – 1955) and (Television: 1950 -1996)
evidence: beginning The Bob Hope Show, sponsored by Pepsodent, on NBC in 1938
Hope's first television appearance was in the "Star Spangled Revue," which aired on Easter Sunday in 1950
His popular television specials, beginning in 1954, would air regularly until 1996.
L28.note: Radio start (1938) and television 1950–1996 are confirmed. The radio end year (1955) is not in this source.

L30.note: “Won an Academy Award 5 times” overstates it. Hope never won a competitive Oscar; his Academy honours were honorary or special awards. Three are on record in the Academy’s own materials: Honorary Award for 1952, Jean Hersholt Humanitarian Award for 1959, Honorary Award for 1965 (the last confirmed here in the Academy’s database). Two more (1940, 1944) are widely reported but were not found in Academy records. IHH’s years (1941, 1945, 1953, 1960, 1966) appear to be ceremony years. Suggested: “Received five honorary and special awards from the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences (never a competitive Oscar)”, once the two 1940s honours are confirmed.

evidence: the memorable Moscow show that won the distinguished Peabody Award in 1958
L31.note: The 1958 Peabody is confirmed by the Television Academy. 1944 and 1968 were not confirmed; the Peabody Awards’ own archive was not retrieved.

evidence: 1958 WINNER Special Achievement Award BOB HOPE
Bing Crosby, Bob Hope, Doris Day
L32.note: The Golden Globes database lists one win for Hope: a 1958 Special Achievement Award. The Golden Globes’ Cecil B. DeMille page names him as a later DeMille awardee, but gives no year, so 1963 is unconfirmed. Suggested: “Golden Globe Special Achievement Award (1958); Cecil B. DeMille Award”, with the year once confirmed.

evidence: the Queen of England made Hope a Knight Commander of the Most Excellent Order of the British Empire in 1998

L46.claim: Honored with Bob Hope Humanitarian Award by the Television Academy (2002)
evidence: First presented to Oprah Winfrey at the 54th Primetime Emmys in 2002, one year before Hope died at age 100
L46.note: The Television Academy’s Bob Hope Humanitarian Award was named for Hope and first presented to Oprah Winfrey in 2002; Hope did not receive it. Suggested: “The Television Academy created the Bob Hope Humanitarian Award in his honour (2002)”. Status revised 17 Oct 2026 from CONFIRMED.

## Biography and captions

**NOT VERIFIED as a whole.** Additional narrative claims to check individually: Cleveland immigration dated 1920 in biography versus 1908 in facts; vaudeville, radio, film and TV career; USO for five decades; over 50 films. Any repeated facts inherit only the scoped evidence above. Interpretive praise is not a verifiable historical fact and should receive editorial review. Image captions and identification remain subject to the item-level rights and identity review in the manifest.

## Proposed biography correction — approval required

**CORRECTION SUGGESTED:** IHH biography immigration year 1920 → 1908. Case Western Reserve’s account says “to Cleveland in March 1908” ([source](https://case.edu/ech/articles/h/hope-leslie-townes-bob), family-arrival paragraph). The IHH facts block already says 1908. This proposal changes no repository profile.
